_comment: TASK-0206. Pin for the vendored fpocket binary that produced the authoritative AUC set (see README.md and RESULTS.md's TASK-0206 section). Regenerate via allostery.baselines.fpocket_provenance('tools/fpocket/bin/fpocket') after any rebuild and diff against this file before trusting a new run.
banner_version_string_caveat: NOT a trustworthy version pin -- this build exposes -P/--custom_pocket (fpocket 4.1's own 'Explicit pocket definition' feature per upstream release notes), so the '4.0' banner is a stale/hardcoded string across the 4.x line, not evidence of which exact tag was built. sha256 above is the only unambiguous pin.
build_recipe: README.md's own pinned recipe: git clone --branch 4.2.3 --depth 1 https://github.com/Discngine/fpocket.git

authoritative_auc_set.note: Re-confirmed reproducible on this machine/binary twice (TASK-0200's own run, and this task's own re-run) -- same-machine determinism holds. Supersedes TASK-0163's original 0.8348/0.8596/0.5345, which this machine/binary cannot reproduce and which cannot currently be re-verified (no access to the machine that produced them from this environment).

superseded_auc_set_TASK_0163.note: Not reproducible on this machine/binary. Root cause: tools/fpocket/bin/ is gitignored (upstream convention) -- only the build recipe is version controlled, never the binary bytes -- so each machine's fpocket is an independently-built, unpinned-until-now artifact. Whether the difference is a genuinely different build (wrong tag / stale local clone predating the README's 4.2.3 pin) or a compiler/architecture-level floating-point difference from nominally the same source was not resolved further (this task's own Constraint explicitly permits pinning without full root-cause). Kept on record, not deleted, per this project's no-overwrite convention.

containerized_build_TASK_0285.platform: linux/amd64 (via Docker Desktop emulation on this arm64 host)
containerized_build_TASK_0285.container_binary_sha256_caveat: Not directly comparable to this file's own native macOS sha256 pin above -- different OS/arch (linux ELF vs macOS Mach-O) means the bytes can never match even for identical source; the comparison that matters is the AUC OUTPUT, not the binary hash, see below.

auc_set.KRAS_G12C: not comparable -- config/targets.yaml's own apo structure changed (4OBE->4LDJ, TASK-0270) after this file's authoritative/superseded pins were recorded, so any KRAS_G12C AUC measured today reflects a different input structure, not fpocket build variance
auc_set.note: Real, decisive finding, not assumed: this containerized build reproduces TASK-0163's own ORIGINAL (superseded) AUCs exactly (0.8596/0.5345), NOT TASK-0206's own re-verified native-rebuild AUCs (0.8618/0.5303) -- on the identical source tag (4.2.3). This is a THIRD independent data point on the same underlying question TASK-0206 first raised, and it does not converge with either prior one. Confirms the drift TASK-0206 found is a genuine build-environment sensitivity (compiler version/flags/qhull behavior), not an artifact of hand-compilation specifically -- Docker with an unpinned-by-digest base image does not fix it either (this build's own first attempt, before the digest pin above was added, is what produced this exact result). Whether the NOW-digest-pinned recipe converges on a stable value across repeated rebuilds, and which of the three AUC sets (if any) a from-scratch multi-machine Docker rebuild would land on, is a real open question -- not resolved further here, flagged as a genuine follow-up. All three AUC sets kept on record, none silently preferred, per this project's own no-overwrite convention.
